title: Telangana Congress holds Samvidhan Raksha March in Hyderabad

tea.why: The Congress party organised the march to express concerns over alleged attempts by the BJP to undermine the Constitution and voting rights.
tea.want: The party demands the protection of constitutional values and the preservation of universal adult franchise.
tea.changed: Nov 26: The march took place in Hyderabad, with Chief Minister Revanth Reddy alleging a conspiracy to delete voters' names.

summary: On November 26, 2026, the Telangana Pradesh Congress Committee organised a 'Samvidhan Raksha March' in Hyderabad to mark Constitution Day. The rally, which followed a call from the All India Congress Committee, began at the Ambedkar statue on Tank Bund and concluded at the Indira Gandhi statue on Necklace Road. Participants included Chief Minister Revanth Reddy, Deputy Chief Minister Mallu Bhatti Vikramarka, and various party officials. Speakers alleged that the BJP is attempting to undermine the Constitution and manipulate electoral processes by deleting voters' names. The event was part of a nationwide series of marches held by the Congress party to advocate for the protection of constitutional principles and voting rights. No official government response to the specific allegations made during the march was reported in the provided sources.
response: No official response reported in the sources.

updates.text: The Samvidhan Raksha March was held in Hyderabad, featuring participation from senior Congress leaders and ministers.
